View all openings View all openings What we're all about Founded in 2017, Retool is where the promise of AI meets trusted enterprise governance. Over 10,000 organizations, including Amazon, Stripe, Brex, and Orangetheory Fitness, operate production-ready software on their business data in Retool. By securely connecting to the databases, APIs, and internal systems enterprises already rely on, Retool ensures every app and automation runs with real data and real permissions—no matter where it was built. Who we are “Who we are” describes us as individuals and as a collective group. We are ambitious - We aim to create massive change, not incremental improvements. We are intensely curious - We ask “why?” so that we can understand root causes, and solve the real problem. We fail fast, we learn fast. We are energetic - We channel energy into action and move things forward. We solve problems with urgency. We care deeply - We hold a high bar for ourselves because we want to have an impact on the things we care about. How we work These describe how we operate at Retool. Obsess over customers - Retool doesn't exist without our customers. Solving for them is at the heart of everything we do. Move uncomfortably fast - We push ourselves to take action, with purpose. Act like an owner - We optimize for Retool's success, not our comfort. Be demanding and supportive - We hold the bar high and help each other clear it. The interview What to expect from our interview process Recruiting processes can feel impersonal and one-sided. We'd like to get to know you, and for you to get to know us. Here's what you can expect from a typical interview loop, though some roles may have more or fewer interviews. 1. Intro calls We start with a couple of conversations — one with your recruiter, one with the hiring manager. Think of these as getting-to-know-you chats where we learn about what you're looking for, share more about the role, and figure out if there's a great mutual fit. Come with questions, we genuinely love them. 2. Technical evaluation or practical exercise This step is all about getting to know you even better and giving you a real window into what the role is actually like. We tailor this stage to focus on the specific skills that matter most for the position, so expect something that closely mirrors the work you'd be doing day-to-day. It's your chance to show us what you've got and get an authentic feel for the job at the same time. *Depending on the role, you may complete this before or after your onsite 3. Onsite Interview You'll complete 3–5 interviews across the team you'd be joining, plus a cross-functional partner or two. Before you get here, we'll walk you through exactly what to expect: who you're meeting, what they care about, and how to put your best foot forward. We want you to feel set up for success, not caught off guard. Set up to help you succeed We believe great work happens when we come together. Our hybrid model brings teams into our San Francisco, New York, Salt Lake City, and London offices to collaborate in person — because shared space fuels creativity, connection, and momentum. Trusted by developers, startups, and the Fortune 500 Trusted by developers, startups, and the Fortune 500 General questions about Retool What can I build in Retool? Apps and automations for the work your business actually runs on, connected to your own data, deployed in your own infrastructure, and governed by your own rules. Most teams use Retool to replace the internal tools they'd otherwise wait months for engineering to build. Who can build in Retool? Anyone who works closely with data and systems: developers, business engineers, analysts, and ops teams. Describe what you need, and the app builder generates a working starting point. Developers can go deeper from there with custom logic, integrations, and component-level control. The builder meets you where you are. What's the difference between builders, internal users, and external users? Enterprise plans can allocate different seat types to reflect how someone uses Retool. Builders are explicitly assigned by admins and can create, edit, and publish apps, workflows, and agents. Internal users are employees who use apps but don't publish changes—they can explore and draft freely without consuming a builder seat. External users are people outside your organization, like partners or clients, who access apps you've built. What's new in Retool's app builder? Retool has entirely rebuilt the app builder from the ground up. The new builder is AI-native: describe what you need, and it generates a working app, connected to your data, that you can refine from there. Apps built in the previous builder continue to work. When you need to distinguish between them, the previous experience is referred to as the classic app builder. How can I deploy Retool? Can I self-host Retool? Retool runs in the cloud or self-hosted in your own VPC. Self-hosted setup takes about 15 minutes via Docker. If your data can't leave your infrastructure, self-hosting is the answer. Enterprise plans support both options. Is Retool secure? Where's my data stored? Retool meets the security and compliance requirements of the most regulated enterprises: role-based access controls, audit logging, SSO, independent workspaces, and full self-hosting. Your queries run against your own data sources. Retool doesn't store your data. See our security documentation for specifics. Do you offer special pricing or discounts for students, educators, or non-profits? Yes, students and educators can apply for a free Business account. Nonprofits can apply for 25 free seats . Both apply to cloud-hosted and self-hosted plans. Frequent questions about AI credits What are AI credits? Every Retool plan includes a monthly pool of AI credits—no add-on, no separate billing. Credits are shared across your organization and cover all app building and AI actions. How many apps can I build? Enough for real work. A Business plan includes credits for 36–84 apps per month. If it helps to think in prompts: each AI prompt uses about 12 credits, and a typical app takes 3–6 prompts to build. Credits cover all app building and AI actions. The pool works across however your team builds. Do credits roll over? Credits renew each billing cycle. The base credits included in your plan are permanent. Bonus credits are included now and may change over time. What happens if we need more credits? Upgrade to a higher tier for more monthly capacity. Additional credit packs are available for purchase to customers on paid plans. Enterprise plan customers can also use their own API key, which does not draw from this pool. Frequent questions about agents What are agents? Agents are AI-powered workers that use large language models to complete tasks, make decisions, and automate workflows autonomously. They are billed hourly and do not draw from the AI credit pool. Why does Retool use hourly pricing for agents? It mirrors how teams already value labor: you pay for productive time, not tokens or runs. Hourly pricing scales with real business value and stays transparent. Why do hourly rates vary by model? Different models have different capabilities. More sophisticated models handle complex reasoning and multi-step execution; lighter models handle simpler tasks efficiently. You choose what matches the job. What types of tasks are best suited for agents? Repetitive, multi-step work: support ticket triage, data analysis and reporting, sales follow-up, security alert handling, research, and workflow orchestration. What counts as agent runtime? Wall-clock time from when an agent starts a task to when it finishes, including executing steps, waiting on API responses, and model processing. Idle time waiting for human input is excluded. What if I’m not sure how many hours I need? Start with the free allocation and use the usage dashboard to track consumption over a few weeks before committing to a paid tier.
